AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: To validate a framework of factors that influence the relationship of transformational leadership and safety climate, and to enable testing of safety chain factors by generating hypotheses regarding their mediating and moderating effects.

AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Understanding the patient safety chain and mechanisms by which leaders affect a strong climate of safety is essential to transformational leadership practice, education, and research.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: A systematic review of leadership and safety literature was used to develop an organising framework of factors proposed to influence the climate of safety. A panel of 25 international experts in leadership and safety engaged a three-round modified Delphi study with Likert-scored surveys.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Eighty per cent of participating experts from six countries were retained to the final survey round. Consensus (>66% agreement) was achieved on 40 factors believed to influence safety climate in the acute care setting.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Consensus regarding specific factors that play important roles in an organisation's climate of safety can be reached. Generally, the demonstration of leadership commitment to safety is key to cultivating a culture of patient safety.

AbstractText.Label: IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING MANAGEMENT
AbstractText.content: Transformational nurse leaders should consider and employ all three categories of factors in daily leadership activities and decision-making to drive a strong climate of patient safety.
